title: $33 for the "Margie" record date
summary: A three-hour record date paid scale of $33, with no royalties though "Margie" sold in the millions.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How about all those (Inaudible) recordings, you get paid extra for the recordings?

Well, recordings in those days, what you got paid for -- a three hour record date in those days was $33.00, and that's it. Now, I made a record of "Margie" with Lunceford on a date, and I got $33.00 for the date, and the record was a big hit. It sold in the millions, this side, "Margie", but I didn't get any more. That was all I got was the $33.00 for making it, just like everybody else who was on that particular date.

And we didn't only make that one side. We'd make four or five or six sides on that date. But that's what I got from it was $33.00. That's what the scale was for recording, and this is what we got. We didn't make much money. We'd play theaters, and we'd make about $75.00 for the week, 75.00, 80.00.
Willie Smith was getting a little more than us, you know, but this was what it was.
How much did the public pay to come in and see?
